note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council on the 27 county electoral divisions, polled on Thursday 3 October 1946: 'Polling took place in county council and rural council elections in Northern Ireland yesterday, with the exception of Co. Londonderry' (Belfast News-Letter, 4 October 1946, p. 3). There were no contests: 'There will be no contests for Tyrone County Council, and in the past 22 years there have only been four contests for the county council' (Belfast News-Letter, 20 September 1946, p. 3). The paper prints every member with his division and the party label in brackets. Uncontested divisions here reflect a deliberate abstention, not missing coverage: in the Omagh Rural District, Nationalists refused to nominate against Unionist-held seats in every year except 1949, when only 4 of 21 such seats were contested (Kingsley 2021, 'The Omagh Rural District Electoral Divisions Scheme 1923', citing PRONI LA/62/2/FA/38 and Ulster Herald 10 Feb 1923). The same pattern is visible across this county's rounds. See notes/tyrone-county-council_absent_contests.txt Returned unopposed.
